correctness.rationale: Exact stationary joint Markov moment recurrence through degree six independently reproduces the cumulants. The Gaussian contribution to cumulants above two vanishes. The sixth/fourth ratio is strictly decreasing with sharp endpoints 32 and 0; its positive algebraic inverse fixes tumbling rate, then fourth and second cumulants fix speed and thermal diffusivity. Positive feasibility is proved necessary and sufficient. A neighborhood construction gives genuine two-cumulant ambiguity. SymPy recurrence, rational example and derivative checks passed.

originality.rationale: The prior beta law and Gaussian convolution already supply all forward moments; those are not novelty claims. The qualified novelty is the complete structural identifiability of three independently unknown physical parameters from the first three nonzero stationary even cumulants, including an exact inverse, a sharp attainable data region and proof of non-identifiability from two. Two closest indexed three-state inverse results are explicitly distinguished by positive residence in a third resting state, calibrated propulsion and absent thermal diffusion. No inspected primary source or available indexed statement covers this same inverse classification. An unindexed general beta-mixture inverse result remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Prior literature gives all forward stationary moments, so this is an inverse theorem of a known family, not a new dynamical solution.
An unindexed general inverse beta-plus-Gaussian moment theorem could pre-empt the global inverse and feasible region.
The indexed finite-tumble results show the general idea of sixth-moment identification is not itself original; novelty is model-specific three-unknown characterization.
Statistical conditioning/measurement noise and physical robustness outside the model are not established.

value.rationale: The naturally motivated inverse problem is to recover speed, heading-switch time and thermal diffusivity from stationary positions in a model used for active-particle measurements. Exact necessary and sufficient constraints on observable cumulants are a falsifiable model check. Sixth-order observations separate active kinetics from Gaussian thermal broadening, and a sharp two-cumulant ambiguity proves genuinely additional information is needed; the fact is not a relabeling of a pre-existing parameter table.
